properties.statement:
⭐ THE FIRST DURABLE CONTENT MIGRATED OUT OF A MACHINE-LOCAL HANDOFF NOTE AND INTO THE GRAPH, under `dec:idea-the-handoff-file-contradicts-an-accepted-decision-and-nobody-reconciled-them`. This is the class of thing that note existed to carry; it is a dated observation about the world, which is what a TemporalFact is, and it now travels with the design instead of living on one laptop.

FIVE WAYS A GREEN SIGNAL WAS FALSE IN ONE SESSION. Three were the agent's OWN command construction, which is the uncomfortable part — the tooling did not lie, the question did.

① **A PIPED GATE REPORTS THE LAST COMMAND'S EXIT CODE.** `cargo test --workspace 2>&1 | grep ... | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20` exited 0 — from `head`. It says NOTHING about cargo. Redirect to a file and read cargo's own exit code.

② **`sort -rn | head -20` HID THE FAILURES IT WAS MEANT TO SURFACE.** A `test result: FAILED` line sorts to the tail by count and is cut. The first "green" workspace run was worthless; the honest re-run reported 157 suites / 1798 passed / 0 failed. **A filter that ranks by frequency buries the rare event, and failures are rare by construction.**

③ **A GREEN `cargo test` IS NOT A GREEN CI.** PR #343's first run failed on `cargo fmt --check` with all 1798 local tests passing. CI's `core` job runs tests → clippy → **Format** → schema → installer → skill lint, and the local habit covered one of six. It also builds `--no-default-features`, a different build from the local `--workspace` run.

④ **`loop_status` REPORTED `state: in_step` ON AN EXPORT FOUR NODES BEHIND.** It means "the file is where the graph left it" — nobody modified it externally — NOT "the graph is exported". The `next` list said the truth in words. Use `compare_designs` for the actual question.

⑤ **`pgrep -f "<command>"` MATCHES ITS OWN WRAPPER**, so "still running" read true after the job had finished. Twice.

🛑 THE PATTERN WORTH KEEPING RATHER THAN THE FIVE INSTANCES: every one of these produced a CONFIDENT, WELL-FORMED, WRONG answer — never an error. `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` exists for exactly this and was available all session; it was broken three times before being consulted. **A trap that returns an error teaches you once. A trap that returns a green tick teaches you nothing, repeatedly.**

📌 STILL IN THE MEMORY NOTE AND NOT YET MIGRATED: `gh pr edit` is broken here (Projects-classic GraphQL — use `gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> --input`); a new MCP tool is uncallable until a client restart; `--stop-shared` leaks a zombie per call. Each is the same genre and each deserves its own node or a shared one.
